title: Déraciné
subtitle: An unseen visitor in frozen time
summary: Déraciné is FromSoftware's virtual-reality adventure, released for PlayStation VR on 6 November 2018.
body: Déraciné is FromSoftware's virtual-reality adventure, released for PlayStation VR on 6 November 2018. The player becomes an unseen faerie in a secluded boarding school, exploring a world suspended in time. Children and objects provide fragments of a mystery that develops as the visitor finds ways to affect their lives. The quiet setting asks for close attention rather than speed: a small alteration to something in the room can become evidence that the invisible being exists and is trying to communicate.

Moving through frozen moments lets the player examine the school and gather information from details that ordinary time would carry past. Objects become a means of reaching the children, who gradually recognize the faerie's presence. The story later shifts through time, making previous discoveries part of understanding another moment. Its central relationship grows through those indirect exchanges. The player occupies the same rooms as the inhabitants while remaining separate from them, a distance that turns observation and intervention into the adventure's principal actions.

Hidetaka Miyazaki and FromSoftware collaborated with Japan Studio on the project, using PlayStation VR and two Move controllers to revisit the measured pace of a traditional adventure. Fragmented storytelling connects the school's mysteries to the bond with its children. Music by Tsukasa Saitoh, Shoi Miyazawa and Yuka Kitamura supports that restrained atmosphere. The headset gives the quiet spaces a physical presence, while the frozen-time premise explains the player's unusual place within them: close enough to notice and change things, but unable simply to join the ordinary flow of life.
